one_line: A browser-local Indonesian tax filing simulator with agent-assisted document and return preparation.
what_it_does: Guides a fictional taxpayer through documents, income, assets, liabilities, family/PTKP, validation, declaration, and simulated receipt while an agent operates structured WebMCP tools and a human approves corrections.
leverage_rationale: State-aware tools can inspect and mutate a multi-step filing workspace, identify inconsistencies, and prepare corrections more reliably than generic UI driving; the human approval boundary is central.
leverage_evidence: About text lists upload, inconsistency finding, navigation, correction preparation, validation, and human-only final review.
Screenshot shows a structured seven-step tax workflow with assets and fictional values.
Base64 document upload workaround demonstrates attention to WebMCP input limitations.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent end-to-end simulated filing scope and a populated workflow, but the supplied evidence is mostly a paused Devpost thumbnail rather than observed execution.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot visibly shows LaporAI filing workspace and Step 3 of 7.
Description enumerates the complete filing sections and simulated receipt.
impact_rationale: Taxpayers facing dense, high-stakes government forms are a concrete audience, and guided verification plus human control directly addresses the problem, even though this is fictional data and a simulation.
impact_evidence: Description identifies Indonesian Coretax-style tax filing and verification needs.
Visible workspace contains assets and financial values with fictional-data notice.
creativity_rationale: A thoughtful human-in-the-loop application of WebMCP to consequential paperwork, with a specific privacy and approval model; the filing category itself is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Agent prepares evidence-based corrections for taxpayer approval rather than submitting autonomously.
Structured document reconstruction addresses missing native file input.
usability_note: Structured step navigation and visible review controls appear usable; detailed interaction is not directly observable.
red_flags: Simulation uses fictional taxpayer data; no live government integration.
No direct readable tool invocation evidence in supplied frames.
standouts: Human-only final reviewer and evidence-based correction workflow.
State-aware filing flow with an explicit file-input workaround.
advance_reason: Strong practical WebMCP fit and credible human-control design, with enough visible product packaging to advance despite limited execution evidence.

one_line: A browser sampler where beatbox recordings become pitch-mapped layers that an agent arranges into a track.
what_it_does: Records microphone audio, turns it into a playable sampler, maps it to keys, generates melodies, suggests complementary layers, and exposes mixing/arrangement controls through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: The product's core novelty is an agent directly manipulating live audio nodes and musical state in the browser; generic UI driving would be substantially less reliable for coordinated capture, mapping, layering, and playback.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly claims live agent tool calls in the browser.
About text enumerates capture_sound, mapping, melody, complementary-layer, tempo, mute, and arrangement tools.
Frame sheet includes a visible music result and asset/studio states, though tool text is small.
execution_rationale: The concept and described mini-DAW scope are coherent, and frames show media/studio-like states, but end-to-end recording-to-track behavior is not fully inspectable.
execution_evidence: Frames show a music/presentation result and populated asset/studio views.
Description specifies Web Audio implementation and a complete flow from capture to arrangement.
impact_rationale: Beatboxers, playful music makers, and novice producers have a clear creative desire that the product addresses immediately; value is primarily expressive and entertainment-oriented.
impact_evidence: Description targets turning any voice or beatbox sound into a playable instrument and arranged track.
Visible featured result communicates a song-generation outcome.
creativity_rationale: The beatbox-to-live-track interaction is memorable and unusually well matched to agent-mediated musical collaboration, combining microphone capture, pitch mapping, and generative arranging.
creativity_evidence: Agent transforms a goofy sound into a layered, playable song in the same browser.
Call-and-response melody and complementary-layer suggestion go beyond a static loop.
usability_note: The described flow is approachable, though microphone permission and complex studio state may add friction.
red_flags: Exact audio quality and live tool sequence are not legible in the supplied frames.
standouts: WebMCP controls meaningful musical state rather than just a button.
advance_reason: Distinctive creative interaction and unusually load-bearing agent surface make this a strong advance candidate.

one_line: A lossless JSON viewer where agents query and point at the exact document and view the human is already using.
what_it_does: Loads large JSON locally, answers bounded queries, reveals paths, highlights matches, filters the viewer, and keeps agent and human state synchronized without copy-paste or uploading the document.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP uniquely lets tools operate on and visibly steer the human's live local viewer: loading the document, revealing paths, flashing rows, and changing reversible view state. A general agent cannot replicate that shared-state loop comparably well.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes load_doc, reveal_path, highlight_matches, and clear_highlights operating in the open viewer.
Transcript says document content is bounded/untrusted and exact int64 values are preserved.
About text explains local worker parsing and UI state shared in one tab.
execution_rationale: The transcript demonstrates a coherent query, highlight, filter, blocked-row, clear-filter, and prompt-injection-handling workflow; frames show document-oriented product states.
execution_evidence: Transcript reports exact failed-delivery counts, row highlighting, filter reversibility, and explicit inability handling.
About text describes bounded schema/query/refine vocabulary and five-million-element support.
Video is 103 seconds and has a dedicated demo title.
impact_rationale: Data-heavy technical users have a real recurring problem locating and discussing faults in large JSON; the shared viewer eliminates a concrete workflow failure and preserves data locally.
impact_evidence: Transcript shows exact query results and navigation to delivery D072 without moving the human's screen.
creativity_rationale: The two-interface/shared-surface concept is a strong original interaction model, especially the reversible visual pointing and injection-safe bounded responses.
creativity_evidence: Agent points at the human's exact document rather than merely describing a result.
Prompt-injection data is treated as untrusted while exact numeric fidelity is retained.
usability_note: The transcript shows clear feedback, reversible filters, graceful inability, and no-copy-paste workflow.
red_flags: Project says its stdio MCP vocabulary was already proven; WebMCP layer is the new transport and shared-view capability.
standouts: Honest failure handling and prompt-injection boundaries are demonstrated.
advance_reason: Best-evidenced and most clearly transformative WebMCP use in the packet.

one_line: A desired-state manager that synchronizes AI-agent skills across machines and agents.
what_it_does: Locks skill versions, compares desired and installed state, detects drift, syncs via Git or cloud, targets agents, and verifies changes through CLI and dashboard workflows.
leverage_rationale: For an agent managing its own distributed skill environment, structured state, exact revisions, drift detection, and verification are materially safer and more precise than generic dashboard automation.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies desired-versus-actual state, exact Git revisions, drift protection, and verification.
WebMCP is part of the cloud dashboard workflow rather than a superficial action.
execution_rationale: The scope is coherent and technically substantial, with CLI, cloud, Git, device, revision, and sync concepts; no video and only screenshot packaging limit end-to-end certainty.
execution_evidence: Description enumerates Git Sync, Cloud dashboard, CLI operations, and drift behavior.
Frame sheets visibly show consistent technical/dashboard states.
impact_rationale: Multi-agent developers have a concrete configuration-drift problem, and exact-version synchronization can prevent broken or inconsistent agent environments.
impact_evidence: Description gives specific Mac/VPS drift scenarios and a desired-state remedy.
Non-managed skills are preserved during normal synchronization.
creativity_rationale: Agent skill fleet management is a timely, ambitious infrastructure concept with thoughtful drift semantics, though desired-state sync is an established pattern.
creativity_evidence: Targets multiple agents and machines, not just package installation.
Adopt, restore, targeting, and safe drift handling deepen the concept.
usability_note: CLI plus dashboard is a sensible operator model; setup and cloud/account details are not evidenced.
red_flags: No submitted video; cloud access model is not clear from packet.
Operational reliability is claimed rather than observed.
standouts: Exact revision locking and non-destructive drift policy.
Useful bridge between agent tooling and fleet operations.
advance_reason: High-value agent-infrastructure problem with a credible, differentiated safety model, though evidence is packaging-heavy.

one_line: A 3D spatial knowledge graph where humans and agents navigate, connect, and synthesize notes.
what_it_does: Turns documents and notes into semantically positioned 3D nodes, supports navigation, paths, clustering, indexing, CRUD, and persistence through a WebMCP co-pilot.
leverage_rationale: Agent control of camera navigation, graph algorithms, and indexing is useful, but a general agent could achieve much of the same through conventional application APIs or UI with friction; shared 3D state adds value but is not fully evidenced.
leverage_evidence: About text lists spatial navigation, BFS learning paths, cluster analysis, and document indexing tools.
No frame sheets were submitted, so live shared-state behavior cannot be checked.
execution_rationale: The concept is ambitious and internally coherent, but there is no video or frame-sheet evidence and the provided description is truncated, capping claimed execution confidence.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot provides only packaging/presentation evidence.
Description names a broad feature set but does not demonstrate completion.
impact_rationale: Researchers, learners, and knowledge workers can benefit from spatial associations and synthesized paths, but practical value depends on the quality of semantic indexing and navigation.
impact_evidence: Description identifies note organization, conceptual bridges, isolated thought islands, and PDF/Markdown indexing.
creativity_rationale: A living 3D knowledge graph with agent co-navigation is a fresh interaction model and ambitious medium choice, even though spatial knowledge tools have precedents.
creativity_evidence: 3D metallic node graph and agent-controlled camera are central to the concept.
Combines graph traversal, clustering, and document chunking into one spatial workspace.
usability_note: 3D navigation may be engaging but could impose cognitive and interaction cost; no usable flow is visible.
red_flags: Broad feature claims lack direct execution evidence.
advance_reason: Creative premise is promising, but the packet lacks the visual and end-to-end evidence required to advance confidently.

one_line: A prompt-injection scanner that screens text, files, URLs, and MCP metadata before content reaches an agent.
what_it_does: Exposes typed WebMCP scans for text, files, public URLs, and MCP servers, returning compact verdicts while keeping candidate content outside model context; includes a Codex repository plugin.
leverage_rationale: The security boundary is meaningful: agents can request bounded pre-context verdicts and opaque file IDs instead of reading hostile content first. WebMCP makes the scanner discoverable in the page, though a conventional API could provide similar scanning.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly positions scanning before the context boundary.
Four typed tools and opaque IDs prevent candidate contents from entering model context.
Frame sheets show structured security/tool-like application panels.
execution_rationale: The product surface and threat model are coherent, with multiple input types and a plugin, but no video and no legible scan report sequence reduce certainty.
execution_evidence: About text specifies scan_text, scan_file, scan_url, and scan_mcp_server.
Visible frames show populated structured application states.
impact_rationale: Prompt injection before model context is a real and increasingly important security problem for agent users, developers, and organizations; the proposed preflight workflow addresses it directly.
impact_evidence: Description names repositories, documents, MCP descriptions, prompts, and resources as hostile-content surfaces.
Scanner covers both individual content and whole repositories via plugin.
creativity_rationale: Moving security inspection before context ingestion and exposing the same security layer to humans and agents is a strong, timely interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Compact verdicts and opaque identifiers enforce a novel privacy/security boundary.
MCP metadata can be inspected without executing capabilities.
usability_note: Typed scan modes and compact verdicts should be operator-friendly; false positives/negatives and model quality are not evidenced.
red_flags: Security efficacy and detection accuracy are not demonstrated.
Hosted backend/provider dependency is mentioned; exact access flow is unclear.
standouts: Pre-context threat screening is sharply scoped.
MCP metadata scanning without execution is a valuable safety feature.
advance_reason: Addresses a concrete agent-safety gap with a credible boundary and meaningful audience, despite limited observed execution.

one_line: A WebMCP privacy boundary that returns allowlisted decisions instead of sensitive values.
what_it_does: Evaluates private predicates locally, gives agents only satisfied/not-satisfied or opaque references, requires human approval for passport verification, logs crossings, and contracts capabilities after review.
leverage_rationale: Page-local evaluation and capability contraction directly exploit WebMCP's in-page boundary; an ordinary agent driving UI would risk exposing raw secrets and cannot reproduce the structured allowlist semantics as reliably.
leverage_evidence: Description states private values remain page-local and agents receive only decisions or opaque references.
Rental and membership scenarios demonstrate reusable predicates.
Boundary Ledger and post-review capability contraction make state transitions explicit.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete, coherent privacy workflow with approval, ledger, withheld values, and post-review state; frames show consistent dark cards/green status states, but no video.
execution_evidence: Description specifies satisfied/withheld outputs, opaque session-bound references, submitted:false, and five-to-two tool contraction.
Frame sheets show multiple consistent populated states.
impact_rationale: Sensitive workflows across finance, identity, health, and age verification need agent assistance without unnecessary disclosure; the demonstrated rental and membership patterns have clear real-world value.
impact_evidence: Description identifies income, passport, age, financial, and health facts as privacy-sensitive.
Human approval is required for passport verification and final submission is intentionally absent.
creativity_rationale: The agent-gets-the-decision-not-the-secret model is a crisp, reusable interaction and security concept, deepened by explicit ledgering and capability contraction.
creativity_evidence: Session-bound opaque references do not encode passport numbers.
Capability surface contracts after sensitive review.
usability_note: Allowlisted outputs and visible ledger reduce ambiguity; the lack of a final submission tool is a deliberate safety boundary.
red_flags: No direct video evidence; security guarantees are described rather than independently tested.
standouts: Human approval and capability contraction are unusually thoughtful.
advance_reason: A strong, reusable WebMCP-native safety pattern with clear impact and coherent execution claims.

one_line: A fully local variant-triage workbench where an agent and human analyze the same genome without upload.
what_it_does: Parses VCF/raw exports in a worker, annotates against a bundled ClinVar subset, offers guided and advanced modes, and exposes read/set/act/explain/history tools over the local analysis.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP enables an agent to operate on sensitive genomic data already loaded in the same tab without uploading it, while sharing filters, selections, explanations, and history with the human.
leverage_evidence: Pitch emphasizes a file that can never be uploaded and same-tab triage.
Description specifies 13 grouped tools and shared guided/advanced analysis state.
Frames show dark technical analysis/console-like states consistent with a variant workbench.
execution_rationale: The implementation description is unusually concrete—worker parsing, variant count, ClinVar subset, two modes, security headers, and tool grouping—and frames show technical product states, though no video.
execution_evidence: Demo genome size and ClinVar subset are explicitly quantified.
Description details guided questions, advanced filters, sorting, manual selection, and history.
Frame sheets visibly show populated technical panels.
impact_rationale: Researchers and privacy-conscious participants have a real need to inspect genomic data without sending it to a service; local analysis directly addresses consent and confidentiality concerns.
impact_evidence: Description grounds the need in narrow consent and unsafe upload practices.
Guided mode explains evidence strength and limitations rather than presenting raw results only.
creativity_rationale: The combination of privacy-preserving local genomics, dual guided/advanced modes, and agent-operated triage is an ambitious and meaningful synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Same-tab human/agent analysis over a non-uploadable file is central.
Tool taxonomy separates read, set, act, explain, and history operations.
usability_note: Guided mode should lower complexity while advanced mode supports experts; genomic interpretation remains inherently demanding.
red_flags: ClinVar subset is bundled and interpretation is not a clinical diagnosis.
No direct agent invocation or end-to-end video evidence.
standouts: Privacy constraint is technically and ethically central, not cosmetic.
Clear dual-mode workflow for novice and expert users.
advance_reason: Strong privacy-native WebMCP use and credible research value with unusually specific implementation evidence.

one_line: A browser piano where an agent turns a learner's request into a playable, visible practice lesson.
what_it_does: Loads pieces, isolates hands, changes tempo, loops bars, adds count-in/metronome, highlights notes, and starts practice through shared WebMCP-controlled piano state.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP converts natural-language pedagogical intent into coordinated instrument state—transport, hand mix, loop, highlights, and practice mode—rather than returning advice the learner must rebuild manually.
leverage_evidence: Description contrasts useful chat advice with inability to reach the piano.
Example request contains multiple coordinated actions and states.
Frames visibly show piano/lesson product imagery, though not tool calls.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a focused and complete lesson workflow with 14 pieces, modes, controls, history, and microphone capture; visible product presentation supports coherence but not full operation.
execution_evidence: Feature list covers transport, slicing, count-in, metronome, highlights, and expected-note practice.
Devpost screenshot visibly presents a piano lesson interface.
Description states the requested lesson becomes immediately playable.
impact_rationale: Piano learners have a clear problem—turning advice into structured practice—and the product delivers a concrete, immediate lesson rather than abstract instructions.
impact_evidence: Audience need is explicitly grounded in practice tasks such as right-hand isolation and bars 1–4 looping.
Includes mouse, touch, and keyboard play plus public-domain pieces.
creativity_rationale: The agent meeting the learner inside a playable instrument is a fresh interaction model, with musical arrangements and practice state treated as first-class shared state.
creativity_evidence: Natural-language multi-action lesson request maps to visible piano state.
Agent-supplied structured musical arrangements and phrase capture extend beyond static tutoring.
usability_note: Clear practice modes and direct playability support learners; microphone permission is optional friction.
red_flags: No submitted video; agent-to-piano interaction is claimed rather than directly shown.
standouts: Strong translation from lesson intent to playable state.
Good fit between agent coordination and instrument controls.
advance_reason: Clear audience value and a compelling shared-state agent interaction, with coherent scope despite limited execution proof.

one_line: An NBA CBA trade co-pilot that diagnoses failed trades and proposes compliant multi-team fixes.
what_it_does: Models 30-team salary-cap trade state, applies complex CBA constraints, routes multi-team deals through exceptions, and uses WebMCP to turn failures into suggested solutions.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools can inspect a large trade canvas and run precise multi-team constraint solving, then mutate the shared state; generic UI automation would be error-prone for the arithmetic and iterative repair loop.
leverage_evidence: Description contrasts existing machines that only say NO with a solver that says how to fix it.
Packet describes second-apron rules, piecewise salary brackets, TPE routing, and roster constraints.
Frames show a populated dark sports/technical dashboard.
execution_rationale: The feature and problem description are detailed and the frames show populated dashboard states, but no video or readable solved trade sequence is supplied.
execution_evidence: Description specifies interactive trade canvas, rule alerts, and three-team balanced trade presentation.
Visible frame sheets show dashboard-like populated states with status coloring.
impact_rationale: Fans, journalists, podcasters, and analysts have a concrete need for accurate, explainable NBA trade exploration; fixing failed trades is directly useful for that audience.
impact_evidence: Description identifies current trade-machine dead ends and manual calculation burden.
Specific examples include a $3.45M error and 29-tab workflow.
creativity_rationale: Turning a trade validator into an autonomous repair co-pilot is a strong new angle on a familiar tool, with ambitious multi-team CBA modeling.
creativity_evidence: System proposes constraint-compliant fixes rather than only validation.
Targets second-apron and multi-team edge cases with a visual canvas.
usability_note: Visual alerts and guided fixes should help non-experts, but the dense CBA domain may remain complex.
red_flags: Claims of 100% legal compliance are not independently verified.
No end-to-end agent invocation or solved trade is directly visible.
standouts: Repair-oriented UX rather than dead-end validation.
advance_reason: Clear audience, differentiated repair workflow, and substantial structured-state opportunity justify advancing, with verification caveats.
